# workspace-box

The workspace's computer: a private desktop and a real VNC screen.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-workspace-box.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-workspace-box.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [store](store.md)

## About

The workspace's computer is a persistent private desktop on this
machine: an X display of its own, a window manager, a browser profile
of its own, and a real VNC server.  It is not a picture of a desktop.
A command started on it consumes its pixels, a click moves its
pointer, a screenshot is the framebuffer it is showing now, and the
app draws the same RFB stream x11vnc sends.

The backend here is `local`: the processes run on the host, in a
private home and on a display no other process uses.  The container
backend in the design is a stronger boundary and has its own task;
this module never pretends the local backend is one.  When the tools
are missing the box is `unavailable` with the names of what is
missing, and every computer method says so rather than drawing a
desk that cannot be touched.

The seam is `workspace/box/*`.  `status` and `vnc` describe the
computer; `start` and `stop` own its lifecycle; `exec`, `screenshot`,
`windows`, `launch`, `clipboard` and the input methods are the hands
the presenter uses; `take-over` and `return-control` hand the screen
between the reviewer and the agent, and an input method refuses while
the reviewer has it.

The screen reaches a client as an RFB socket, through the
`scripts/workspace-box/websockify.py` bridge and the noVNC page under
`scripts/workspace-box/novnc`.  The app speaks RFB itself; the page is
for a browser, and the same port serves both.

The box outlives the chat and a harness restart: its record and the
pids are kept under the state directory, and a running box is adopted
by its pids when the module starts.  `reset` throws its home away;
`stop` keeps it.

## Provides

### Methods

- `workspace/box/browser` (workspace) — Return WORKSPACE's browser profile resources, metadata only.
- `workspace/box/click` (workspace x y &optional opts) — Click at X, Y on WORKSPACE's screen.
- `workspace/box/clipboard` (workspace &optional text) — Read WORKSPACE's clipboard, or write TEXT to it.
- `workspace/box/drag` (workspace from to) — Drag the pointer on WORKSPACE's screen from FROM to TO.
- `workspace/box/exec` (workspace command &optional opts) — Run COMMAND in WORKSPACE's computer.
- `workspace/box/key` (workspace key &optional opts) — Press KEY on WORKSPACE's screen.
- `workspace/box/launch` (workspace what) — Open WHAT on WORKSPACE's computer.
- `workspace/box/logs` (workspace &optional lines) — Return the last LINES of workspace WORKSPACE's box logs.
- `workspace/box/reset` (workspace &optional keep-home) — Stop WORKSPACE's computer and clear its home unless KEEP-HOME.
- `workspace/box/restart` (workspace) — Stop and start WORKSPACE's computer.
- `workspace/box/return-control` (workspace) — Return control of WORKSPACE's computer to the agent.
- `workspace/box/screenshot` (workspace &optional opts) — Return a PNG of WORKSPACE's current screen.
- `workspace/box/scroll` (workspace x y amount) — Scroll at X, Y on WORKSPACE's screen by AMOUNT clicks.
- `workspace/box/start` (workspace) — Start WORKSPACE's computer, or return it when it already runs.
- `workspace/box/status` (workspace) — Return the state of WORKSPACE's computer.
- `workspace/box/stop` (workspace) — Stop WORKSPACE's computer; its home and browser profile stay.
- `workspace/box/take-over` (workspace) — Give the reviewer control of WORKSPACE's computer.
- `workspace/box/type` (workspace text) — Type TEXT into the window focused on WORKSPACE's screen.
- `workspace/box/vnc` (workspace) — Return the VNC endpoint of WORKSPACE's computer.
- `workspace/box/windows` (workspace) — Return the windows open on WORKSPACE's screen.
- `workspace/browser/clear` (id scope &optional origin kinds) — Clear browser data in workspace ID and return the resources answer.
- `workspace/browser/login/forget` (id login) — Forget the saved site session LOGIN in workspace ID.
- `workspace/browser/open` (workspace url &optional opts) — Open URL in WORKSPACE's browser and return what was opened.
- `workspace/browser/screenshot` (workspace &optional opts) — Return a PNG of WORKSPACE's screen for the browser.

### Events

- `workspace/box-status` — (WORKSPACE STATUS) when a workspace computer changed state.

### Options

- `harness-workspace-box-autostart-browser` — Whether starting the box opens the local start page in its browser.
- `harness-workspace-box-backend` — Which backend a workspace computer uses.
- `harness-workspace-box-browser` — The browser started in the box for a URL, or nil for none.
- `harness-workspace-box-exec-timeout` — Seconds a foreground box command may take before it is stopped.
- `harness-workspace-box-height` — Height of the workspace computer's screen, in pixels.
- `harness-workspace-box-output-limit` — Most characters of a box command's output that is returned.
- `harness-workspace-box-screenshot-timeout` — Seconds a screenshot may take.
- `harness-workspace-box-tool-directories` — Extra directories to look in for the box's tools.
- `harness-workspace-box-tools` — The tools the local box needs before it can start.
- `harness-workspace-box-web-root` — The noVNC directory served by the box, or nil for the bundled one.
- `harness-workspace-box-width` — Width of the workspace computer's screen, in pixels.
- `harness-workspace-box-window-manager` — Window managers tried in order, when one is present.

## Uses

### Methods it calls

- `store/delete` ([store](store.md))
- `store/list` ([store](store.md))
- `store/load` ([store](store.md))
- `store/save` ([store](store.md))
- `workspace/get` ([workspace](workspace.md)), when it is loaded
- `workspace/resources/status` ([workspace](workspace.md))

### Events it handles

- `workspace/deleted` → `harness-workspace-box--on-workspace-deleted`

### Events it emits

- `workspace/box-status`
- `workspace/changed`
